s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with transient complete atrioventricular block
salient_findings: Gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
key_facts: Patient in their late 40s
Admitted for uterine myomectomy procedure
No history of structural heart disease
No history of hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
No family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
No pharmacologic agents affecting cardiac rhythm
Normal laboratory tests
Normal initial 12-lead ECG
Normal chest radiographic imaging
Normal echocardiographic findings
Holter monitor recording showed ventricular asystole during syncope
Electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system

shortlist.label: Paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a transiently suspended asystole by a spontaneous junctional escape beat, suggesting vagal influence

shortlist.label: Neurally mediated syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and Holter monitor recording are consistent with neurally mediated syncope, which can cause transient complete atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and lack of structural heart disease make vasovagal syncope a plausible diagnosis, and it can cause similar symptoms to paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Idiopathic complete atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's normal electrophysiologic studies and lack of underlying heart disease make idiopathic complete atrioventricular block a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's Holter monitor recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block, which is consistent with vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block.

rejected.label: Neurally mediated syncope
rejected.why: Too broad and does not specifically address the atrioventricular block

rejected.label: Vasovagal syncope
rejected.why: Typically involves a drop in blood pressure and heart rate, but the primary issue here is atrioventricular block

rejected.label: Idiopathic complete atrioventricular block
rejected.why: Does not account for the transient and vagus-mediated nature of the block
